root.name: Réti Opening: Anglo-Slav Variation, Bogoljubow Variation

overview: White builds a Réti set-up with b3, Bb2 and a g3 or e3 fianchetto against Black's Slav-style ...c6/...d5 centre. Black usually plays ...Nf6, ...e6 and ...Be7, or ...Bf5 (New York System); the centre stays in tension and the game is a slow manoeuvring fight. Chances are level and play depends on timely central breaks.

white_ideas.idea: Fianchetto both bishops and press the long diagonal, then play d4 or cxd5
Keep e3/d3 flexible and choose a Stonewall or Catalan-type set-up
Break with d4 or c4xd5 when Black commits

black_ideas.idea: Develop the light bishop outside the pawn chain with ...Bf5
Break with ...c5 or ...e5 to challenge the centre

typical_structures.structure: Slav-type c6/d5 pawns against c4/b3 with both sides fianchettoing
Stonewall-style pawns on d4/e3/c3/f4 when White plays e3

character.notes: Slow positional manoeuvring, hard to lose for either side.

structure.notes: Tension in the centre, nothing locked or exchanged early.

approach.notes: Réti-style piece set-up against the Slav; played by strong players but not a universal system.

level.notes: Clear fianchetto plans but flexible move orders to learn.

sublines_that_differ.name: Stonewall Line
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. Nf3 d5 2. c4 e6 3. g3 Nf6 4. Bg2 Be7 5. O-O O-O 6. b3 c6 7. Bb2
sublines_that_differ.how: A closed Stonewall-like structure after a different move order.

character.reason: Slow, symmetrical fianchetto play with few early tactics.

structure.reason: Centre stays in tension in a Réti-style flank opening.

approach.reason: A named line against the Slav, not a universal system.

level.reason: Plans are clear but move orders vary.

plans.reason: Both bishops on the long diagonals, centre contested from the flank.
